kata.name: Builder as monoid — near-floor control: a one-step builder where the conventional accumulation diff catches every injected fault
kata.series_report: beads catherine-lgl.2 (pattern-kata: Builder as monoid); docs/ref/ploeh-grounding.md §6 (HYPOTHESIZED candidate, no series run); pre-registered in fixtures/katas/builder-monoid/README.md
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: at the one-step floor a conventional sampled accumulation check catches both the dropped and the duplicated step; the lens must add nothing (control killed)

expected.detail: the one-step builder loses its only step; the conventional sampled diff names the missing step and the probe reports a dangling part_step cell for the same fault — parity, not a lens win

a duplicate second step changes the one-step accumulation; the conventional diff catches it, while path equations cannot state instance multiplicity — the control's zero-unique outcome is recorded, never forced into a lens finding

commands: python3 prototype/builder_monoid_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: baseline arm frozen; floor faults caught
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/builder-monoid/floor/single-step-builder.ct.json --json  # exit 0, findings []
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/builder-monoid/floor/faults/01-dropped-step.ct.json --json  # exit 4, 1 dangling
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/builder-monoid/floor/faults/02-duplicated-step.ct.json --json  # exit 0, findings []

comparison.conventional_baseline: scripted accumulation diff over sampled steps: the recorded trace is replayed and each sampled step row's existence and emitted part are asserted; the schema map and redundancy declarations are outside the conventional runtime test's vocabulary. At the one-step floor both faults are fully visible to it.

baseline.artifact: prototype/builder_monoid_baseline.py sha256:9d7b1066b77e9feedef981a4e1711a1af691ad99958cedeea5c2ec0408ef9ff4 (scripted accumulation diff over sampled steps)

expressibility_gap.invariant: a step appears at most once in the accumulation (instance multiplicity)
expressibility_gap.why: path equations relate arrow compositions, not multiplicities; the one-step floor's duplicate is caught only by the conventional diff

discrepancies: Control scope: this control demonstrates parity at the one-step floor. It does not replace the above-floor identity/default law (empty build = documented defaults), which has no path-equation form over an instance and is recorded as a gap, not tested here.
procedure: 1. The fault set and its expectations were committed in fixtures/katas/builder-monoid/ (README.md, faults.json) before any run; nothing here is edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/builder_monoid_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: a scripted accumulation diff over the pre-registered sampled step indices; it never inspects a schema_map and never runs the redundancy analysis. Its detections and canonical identified elements are frozen assertions.
3. The probe arm ran the committed fixtures through the real CLI: catherine check (violations/dangling), catherine migrate (lost rows/cells), and catherine redundant (derivable declarations).
4. Elements were compared, not prose: each probe witness is mapped to a canonical fault element by the pre-registered probe_element_map; the baseline's detections are mapped by baseline_element_map.

5. unique_detections = probe canonical elements minus baseline-identified elements, computed by prototype/builder_monoid_baseline.py; an empty unique set is killed, a non-empty set with the executed arm is survived.
